title: Cheesy Korean Corn Fritters
subtitle: with Spicy Seoul Sauce and Spring Onion
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Thinly slice the spring onion. Drain and rinse the corn. Coarsely grate the cheese.

Make batter: Put 10g butter in a large microwave-safe bowl and microwave for 20 secs or until melted. Add 200ml milk and 2 eggs to the butter and whisk until combined. Add the pancake mix, season generously with salt and whisk until just combined. (For light pancakes, don't over-mix.) Gently fold in the corn, cheese and a pinch of shichimi togarashi (see Make it milder).
Make spicy sauce: Combine the chilli paste (see Make it milder) and 1½ tbs mayonnaise in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.

Cook corn fritters: Brush a large frypan with some of the vegetable oil, then heat over medium heat. For each fritter, pour ⅓ cup of the batter into the pan. Cook for 1-2 mins until bubbles appear. Turn the fritters and cook for a further 30 secs or until golden underneath. Transfer to a plate and cover to keep warm. Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly oiling the pan between batches.

Serve up: Meanwhile, put the spinach in a bowl, drizzle with 2 tsp vegetable oil, season with salt and pepper and toss to combine. Divide the corn fritters among plates. Scatter with the spring onion and a pinch of shichimi togarashi, if desired. Serve with the spicy sauce and dressed spinach. Enjoy!

Make it milder: Shichimi togarashi is a fiery seasoning also known as Japanese seven-spice. If you aren't keen on too much heat, serve it at the table for those who like it. ~ Korean chilli paste, also known as gochujang, is a staple in every Korean pantry. It is slightly sweet, earthy and has a chilli kick. Reduce to taste if you prefer less heat.
